title: Designing Informative Thermal Performance Experiments
text: Thermal performance curves (TPCs) describe measure performance (growth, fecundity, survival, etc.) changes temperature. Fitting TPC requires choosing temperatures measure performance , choice matters: temperatures clustered uninformative part curve (e.g., near thermal optimum) can leave edges curve – critical thermal minimum maximum – poorly estimated, even large sample size. TPCdesign helps choose experimental temperatures maximally informative fitting Brière-2 TPC, given rough prior guess curve’s shape. vignette walks full workflow: Define Brière-2 TPC using rough prior guesses parameters. Use design_temps() choose informative temperatures curve. Simulate data true curve temperatures sim_gamma_data(). Fit simulated data check well true parameters recovered, compared naive, equally-spaced set temperatures.

title: Designing Informative Thermal Performance Experiments
text: Brière-2 curve parameterized lower thermal limit (ctmin), upper thermal limit (ctmax), shape parameters b. briere2_tpc() evaluates curve, briere2_tpc_Topt() returns thermal optimum:  practice, never know parameters exactly ahead time – rough guesses, exactly design_temps() built work .
code: true_ctmin <- 8 true_ctmax <- 38 true_a <- 1 true_b <- 0.2  temp_grid <- seq(true_ctmin, true_ctmax, length.out = 200) perf <- briere2_tpc(temp_grid, true_ctmin, true_ctmax, true_a, true_b) topt <- briere2_tpc_Topt(true_ctmin, true_ctmax, true_b)  plot(temp_grid, perf, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "dodgerblue4",     xlab = "Temperature", ylab = "Performance",     main = "Brière-2 thermal performance curve") abline(v = topt, lty = 2, col = "grey50")

title: Designing Informative Thermal Performance Experiments
text: design_temps() takes best guess ctmin, ctmax, , b, along uncertain ctmin, ctmax, b (ctmin_err, ctmax_err, logb_err, respectively), searches set temperatures expected informative across range plausible curves. ask 6 temperatures, treating guesses uncertain degrees: comparison, naive design might just space temperatures evenly across range:  Note optimized design concentrates temperatures near ctmax, curve changing quickly therefore informative curve actually crosses zero, naive design spreads temperatures regard curve’s shape.
code: set.seed(1)  opt_temps <- design_temps(     n_temps = 6,     ctmin = true_ctmin, ctmax = true_ctmax, a = true_a, b = true_b,     ctmin_err = 2, ctmax_err = 1.5, logb_err = 0.26,     n_draws = 100L, n_starts = 3L, n_filler = 1L ) opt_temps #> [1] 11.25 18.98 26.70 34.39 36.40 38.41 naive_temps <- round(seq(true_ctmin + 1, true_ctmax - 1, length.out = 6), 2) naive_temps #> [1]  9.0 14.6 20.2 25.8 31.4 37.0

what: Does the optimized design actually help?
title: Designing Informative Thermal Performance Experiments
text: check whether optimized temperatures worth using, can simulate data designs fit Brière-2 curve back dataset, compare precisely true parameters recovered. requires nls.multstart package, section skipped isn’t installed: simulation, estimates optimized design closer true parameter values, standard errors noticeably smaller – especially ctmax b, optimized design samples much densely near curve’s upper edge. practical benefit using design_temps(): number temperatures replicates, resulting fit precise.
code: dat_naive <- sim_gamma_data(naive_temps, n_reps = 6L, obs_cv = 0.15,                             ctmin = true_ctmin, ctmax = true_ctmax,                             a = true_a, b = true_b)  # Search bounds for starting values, matching how uncertain we said we # were when calling design_temps() above. These must be given in the same # order the parameters first appear in the model formula below # (a, ctmin, ctmax, b). b_bounds <- exp(log(true_b) + c(-1, 1) * 0.26) start_lower <- c(a = 0.5, ctmin = true_ctmin - 2, ctmax = true_ctmax - 1.5,                  b = b_bounds[1]) start_upper <- c(a = 1.5, ctmin = true_ctmin + 2, ctmax = true_ctmax + 1.5,                  b = b_bounds[2])  fit_tpc <- function(dat) {     nls.multstart::nls_multstart(         y ~ a * temp * pmax(temp - ctmin, 0) * pmax(ctmax - temp, 0)^b,         data = dat, iter = 100,         start_lower = start_lower, start_upper = start_upper,         supp_errors = "Y", convergence_count = 30     ) }  fit_opt <- fit_tpc(dat_opt) fit_naive <- fit_tpc(dat_naive)  comparison <- rbind(     truth = c(a = true_a, ctmin = true_ctmin, ctmax = true_ctmax, b = true_b),     `optimized estimate` = coef(fit_opt),     `optimized SE` = summary(fit_opt)$coefficients[, "Std. Error"],     `naive estimate` = coef(fit_naive),     `naive SE` = summary(fit_naive)$coefficients[, "Std. Error"] ) round(comparison, 3) #>                        a ctmin  ctmax     b #> truth              1.000 8.000 38.000 0.200 #> optimized estimate 1.173 5.992 36.467 0.079 #> optimized SE       0.100 2.918  0.174 0.054 #> naive estimate     0.479 9.643 42.317 0.482 #> naive SE           0.612 2.393  6.971 0.434

title: Design Informative Thermal Performance Experiments
text: Fitting thermal performance curve (TPC) requires choosing temperatures measure performance . Temperatures placed uninformative parts curve can leave critical thermal minimum maximum poorly estimated, even many replicates. TPCdesign chooses experimental temperatures expected informative fitting Brière-2 TPC, given rough prior guesses curve’s parameters uncertain . optimization uses approximate coordinate exchange acebayes package. Main functions: design_temps(): choose informative temperatures. briere2_tpc() briere2_tpc_Topt(): evaluate Brière-2 curve thermal optimum. sim_gamma_data(): simulate performance data set temperatures.

title: Design experimental temperatures — design_temps
text: n_temps Single integer total number temperatures return, including filler temperatures added via n_filler. Must >= 2. ctmin Single numeric best guess curve's critical thermal minimum, .e., lower temperature performance reaches zero. Used center uniform prior ctmin (see ctmin_err). ctmax Single numeric best guess curve's critical thermal maximum, .e., upper temperature performance reaches zero. Used center uniform prior ctmax (see ctmax_err). Must > ctmin. Single numeric best guess Brière-2 curve's parameter, scales overall magnitude performance. Unlike ctmin, ctmax, b, treated known exactly (corresponding *_err argument) since shape optimal design insensitive . Must > 0. b Single numeric best guess Brière-2 curve's b parameter, controls asymmetry (skew) curve ctmin ctmax. Used center uniform prior log(b) (see logb_err). Must > 0. ctmin_err Single numeric uncertain ctmin. means priors ctmin generated uniform distribution minimum ctmin - ctmin_err maximum ctmin + ctmin_err. Larger values reflect less confidence ctmin guess cause design hedge across wider range possible curves. Must >= 0. Defaults 2.50. ctmax_err Single numeric uncertain ctmax. means priors ctmax generated uniform distribution minimum ctmax - ctmax_err maximum ctmax + ctmax_err. Larger values reflect less confidence ctmax guess cause design hedge across wider range possible curves. Must >= 0. Defaults 1.50. logb_err Single numeric uncertain b, expressed log scale. means priors log(b) generated uniform distribution minimum log(b) - logb_err maximum log(b) + logb_err. Larger values reflect less confidence b guess cause design hedge across wider range possible curve shapes. Must >= 0. Defaults 0.26. min_sep Single numeric specifying minimum separation (temperature units) enforced optimized temperatures, avoid wasting experimental effort temperatures close together useful. step equally-spaced temperatures added (happens n_filler >= 1) affected argument, unless number points high relative difference maximum (ctmax + ctmax_err) minimum (ctmin + ctmin_err) temperatures surveyed, minimum separation change step anyway. Defaults 2. n_filler Single integer specifying many n_temps total temperatures equally spaced (chosen fill largest gaps left optimized temperatures) rather individually optimized. Equally spacing points can good bet hedging strategy quite unsure TPC parameters (ctmin, ctmax, , b) using, since guards optimization overfitting misspecified curve. Must 0 n_temps. Defaults 1L. n_draws Single integer specifying number Monte Carlo draws taken priors ctmin, ctmax, b approximate expected information gained candidate design. Increase certainty low (.e., *_err parameters high), since wider priors need draws well approximated. Larger values give accurate (slower) optimization. Defaults 250L. n_starts Single integer specifying number independent random starting designs coordinate-exchange optimization run , best-performing result across starts returned. Increasing reduces chance optimizer settles locally (rather globally) optimal set temperatures, cost computation; cost can mitigated running starts parallel (see Examples). Defaults 7L. digits Single integer specifying number decimal places round returned temperatures . Defaults 2L. min_temp Single numeric specifying minimum possible value design temperatures allow. NULL (default), set ctmin - ctmin_err. Must <= ctmin. max_temp Single numeric specifying maximum possible value design temperatures allow. NULL (default), set ctmax + ctmax_err. Must >= ctmax.
